The story achieves an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition, using each element effectively to serve its narrative span of a full year. Because the plot covers a slow, grinding bureaucratic and construction process from October to the following October, the author appropriately uses summary to compress time, explain the history of the building, and convey the contents of endless administrative emails. However, to prevent the narrative from feeling dry, the author grounds each month's progression in brief, vivid scenes—such as the open meeting with the facilities director, the moment a student catches Vale's splitting grocery bag of books, the worker photographing the mold, and the February faculty meeting. This interplay allows the reader to feel the drawn-out exhaustion of the repairs (through summary) while still experiencing the immediate frustrations and absurdities of the characters' daily lives (through scenes).
